title: fix: stabilize CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and warmup scheduling
author: Samira Patel
description:
Context: Recent rollout of CUDA graph capture/replay introduced intermittent failures during warmup when dynamic shape guards and the warmup scheduler interacted. Symptoms included incorrect graph replays, stale KV-cache state for some sequences, occasional OOMs, and degraded latency tail. This PR fixes scheduling and state-management edgecases to stabilize capture/replay across warmup cycles and shape guard transitions.

Motivation: Ensure deterministic graph replays across warmup and shape-guard boundaries so that continuous batching and KV cache remain consistent and we avoid silent regressions in inference latency/throughput. This surfaced in internal perf canaries (see ENG-4123) and a customer incident (SUP-1876).

What I changed (high level):
- Scheduler: reworked warmup scheduler enqueue/dequeue to avoid capturing incomplete KV-cache states when shape guards flip during warmup. Added explicit capture barrier before replaying graphs for sequences that changed shape during warmup cycles.
- Shape guards: tightened guard lifecycle so that graph capture respects the active guard set and invalidates captures deterministically when guards change.
- KV cache sync: ensured KV-cache snapshotting happens atomically with capture; added lightweight epoch counters to avoid stale replays.
- Replay validation: added a verification pass in debug builds that replays a captured graph with a dry-run check to detect mismatches early. Disabled by default in release builds.
- Tests: added unit + integration tests for guard transitions, warmup scheduling, and a canary workload simulating continuous batching with mixed sequence lengths.

Why this fixes it: The root cause was a race between the warmup scheduler and the shape-guard invalidation path that could allow a capture to proceed with a guard set that was stale by the time replay happened. By introducing a capture barrier and atomic KV-cache snapshot semantics, replay now deterministically fails-fast and falls back to non-graph path until a new valid capture completes.

Rollout plan: Merge to main behind a runtime feature gate (cuda_graph_safe_mode). Enable in dedicated canary clusters first, monitor latency tails and OOM counts, then enable globally. See release_notes for details.

Related: references to previous work and regressions: pr-26234, pr-25689, ENG-4123, SUP-1876.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for scheduler/guard interactions
- [x] Integration canary test with continuous batching
- [x] CI green locally and on main
- [x] Documented feature gate and diagnostics

Notes: This change is intentionally conservative — it favors correctness over capturing every possible optimization until we can validate safety across more workloads.

merge_details: Squash commit: 'fix: stabilize CUDA graph capture/replay with shape guards and warmup scheduling' — merged by Priya Rao
release_notes:
- Fixed: Stabilize CUDA graph capture/replay when shape guards change during warmup (avoids OOMs and incorrect replays).
- Improved: atomic KV-cache snapshotting during capture to prevent stale replays.
- Added: debug replay validator and canary tests for warmup + shape guard transitions.
Deployment: Feature gated (cuda_graph_safe_mode). Enable in canary clusters and monitor latency/OOM metrics before broad rollout.
notes_for_changelog: Stability fix for CUDA graph capture/replay under mixed-length workloads and shape-guard transitions. Backwards-compatible; controlled by feature gate.
manual_test_instructions: 1) Enable feature gate 'cuda_graph_safe_mode' in runtime config. 2) Deploy to canary cluster. 3) Run benchmarks/continuous_batching_mixed_lengths.yaml for 30 minutes. 4) Monitor metrics: runtime.graph.capture_failures, runtime.kv.epoch_mismatch, infra.memory.oom_count. 5) If capture_failures > 0 consistently, collect debug replay traces and revert gate.
performance_impact_summary: Minor p50 regression (~1-3%) when fallback to non-graph path occurs frequently; significant reduction in p99 and elimination of intermittent OOMs in affected workloads.
qa_notes: Added new unit + integration tests. QA should validate on dedicated canary with mixed-length workload and verify no regressions in continuous batching throughput.
